hero.heading: Make All Science Open Science
hero.lead: Gathering for Open Science Hardware (GOSH) is a movement that aims to disrupt the way that scientific tools are designed, produced, and used, with the goals of accelerating scientific discovery and making science more accessible and inclusive.

hero_more.markdown:
Building on the work of previous GOSH events held in [Switzerland](../gosh-2016) (2016), [Chile](../gosh-2017) (2017), and [China](../gosh-2018) (2018), regionally focused events are lower cost and focus on accomplishing the [work laid out by the Global GOSH community](https://gitlab.com/gosh-community/gosh-roadmap/boards), [manifesto](../gatherings/gosh-manifesto) and [roadmap](../gatherings/global-open-science-hardware-roadmap). International applicants are encouraged to apply, but be aware there are very limited funds for travel and visa support available.

The event will take place from July 31-August 2, 2019 at the University of Toronto and [Evergreen Brick Works](https://www.evergreen.ca/), a community hub with a mission to promote “sustainable practices that enable flourishing cities of the future”.

The cost of the event ($300 full, $150 discounted) includes food and lodging for 3 nights, and accepted applicants who cannot pay will be provided support to cover the cost. So apply at whatever level works for you!

A [post-even Hackathon](../gatherings/great-lakes-gosh-2019/2019-gl-gosh-hackathon/) will focus on collaborative and application oriented open hardware hacking. Connect to some existing project ideas, or bring your own and find collaborators.
